definitions.name: opt-in decision callbacks receive bounded current task text without leaking it into status or ordinary diagnostics
decision sink failures and pending writes never delay or change the upstream stream
a fallback decision is logged even when its upstream request fails
client cancellation closes the upstream stream

assertion_order_scope: Raw successful assertion order retained separately. Per-site and per-callback counts are exact; no scheduling or chunk partition equivalence is inferred.
network_scope: Actual synthetic gateway/provider loopback HTTP using the original supplied route callbacks. No real evaluator calls.
capture_semantics: Complete selected callbacks and five helper statements restored unchanged except successful assertion-result wrappers. Recording delegates actual HTTP and original return objects; no clone/drain, substituted verdict, timing threshold or source clock changes. Per-peer complete bodies preserve actual parser-delivered bytes; raw push chunks and chronological reads remain in raw observations. Provider request bodies remain unread by the original callbacks. Every original seven-variant privacy assertion, decision-sink throw/returned rejection/never-ready Promise, fallback outcome and actual response.body.cancel remains intact. The capture observes delegated body cancellation completion and actual upstream response close separately. All injected 12.25/0.5/1/1501 decision latencies remain exact; generated timestamps and actual measured transport timings stay raw with only declared stability projections. The status callback Promise catch method is observed only when the original safe emitter installs and executes its own handler; the recorder never adds a detached rejection handler. Asynchronous assertions are counted only after their original Promise resolves successfully.
typed_observations: Headers inputs are enumerated into their complete normalized field map.
Route signal observation records actual AbortSignal type and aborted state; no serialized object identity is claimed. countTokens is recorded as a function capability only.
Individual response chunks remain base64, including intentionally split UTF-8. Only complete request bodies use UTF-8 after exact roundtrip validation.
